reason: Fixed. Media type is not stored and is not taken from the upstream Content-Type. The route sniffs the downloaded bytes against the four allowed signatures (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) and serves the sniffed type; bytes that match none return 502. The hash check runs first, so sniffing only ever sees the bytes that were read.

Fixed; this was a precondition, not an open question. Attachments get their own reader setting, `NEXUS_ATTACHMENT_VISION_MODEL`, mapped through the same `VISION_BACKENDS` table. Unset means attachments are refused with 503, not that they fall back to the ingest model. `vision_model()` and the ingest `extractor_identity()` are untouched, so switching the attachment reader never re-keys ingest. The open question is removed.

Fixed. Invariant: the image is served only if the principal can read at least one chunk in that tenant whose marker carries the handle, and the check runs over all such chunks, not one picked chunk. The bytes are identical for every chunk carrying the handle, so a principal who can read one of them already sees text read from those bytes; serving the image discloses nothing beyond that chunk. Otherwise 404.

Checked on master: `search_text` is recorded only as length and hash (`search/signals.py:153-157`, `search_text_len`, `search_text_sha256`); query-text retention stores `req.query`, not `search_text` (`api.py:952`). So image text that reaches search through `search_text` is not stored. The SPEC now states this in §3, states the invariant (no retention path receives the image text: search log, query-text retention, rewrite record, stage spans), and §7 tests each of them.

Fixed. Machine-read caller material is kept apart from typed caller material: `validate_numbers` gains a fourth source, `attachment`, so a number found only in the image text reports `found_in = attachment`, never `context`. In the prompt the image text has its own labelled block stating it was machine-read from the caller's image, separate from `answer_context`.
Fixed by the same change as I-005: `validate_numbers` takes `attachment` as its own argument, so `answer_context` and image text are checked separately and neither replaces the other.

Correct: `web/js/api.js` authenticates with an `Authorization: Bearer` header, which an `` request does not send. Thumbnails are fetched with the same header, turned into a blob and shown through an object URL. The CSP keeps `blob:` and drops `data:`.

Fixed. The cap is enforced on bytes read, not on the header: a small wrapper on the two answer routes counts body bytes as they arrive and stops with 413 at the cap, with or without `Content-Length`. A declared `Content-Length` over the cap is rejected before reading.
Fixed. On the stream route, decoding, `read_image` and `scan_content` finish before the response starts, so 413, 422, 502 and 503 are real HTTP statuses. §7 tests them on the stream route as well.

Fixed. Concurrent requests for the same handle share one upstream fetch; upstream work is bounded by a per-process limit (proposed 4) and a timeout (proposed 10 seconds), over which the route returns 503 with a retry hint. When no Notion token is configured (`NOTION_TOKEN`, the variable the Notion source reads), the route returns 503 'source resolution not configured' and the UI shows that text. A rate limit per principal is not added here.

Partly. A second row for one handle is prevented by the unique index `idx_vision_handle` on `(tenant, left(image_sha256, 16), extractor_identity)` (migration 016), so a 64-bit collision fails at ingest rather than at view time; `AmbiguousHandle` at view time therefore means the index is missing or broken, and 500 stays. What changes: the reader is told ('the image reference is ambiguous; it cannot be shown'), not only the log.

Fixed. The backstop reread now covers the connector: the route reuses the existing Notion source's block read, at request time, and adds no new source or connector. The proposed ruling stays does-not-fire, with that stated.

Fixed. §7 adds a test on the attachment path itself: the request it sends has no tool definitions (Anthropic backend), the bridge call uses `/v1/vision` with the argv closed by `_DOORS_CLOSED`, and the reader receives bytes, never a path.

Fixed. The header is set only on the web UI routes (`/` and `/static`), not app-wide, and it is a full policy, not `img-src` alone. The policy is defined once, by one helper, and is the same string in this SPEC and SPEC-nexus-answer-visuals; `data:` is dropped (I-007).

Fixed. Acceptance requires the thumbnail step; without a Notion token the SPEC is not accepted yet, rather than accepted with the step skipped. First use gets an observable record: the improvement-loop hand run records how many questions carried an image and how many thumbnails were opened, in that run's record. No date is set because the loop's hand run has none; that is stated.
